name: Dien Bien Phu
provinceNote: Điện Biên province stayed in place. Resolution 202/2025/QH15 left it unchanged, and the statistics office catalog prints “Giữ nguyên, không sắp xếp” for the province. Resolution 1661/NQ-UBTVQH15 of 16 June 2025, in force 1 July 2025, merged the old wards Him Lam, Tân Thanh, Mường Thanh, Thanh Bình, and Thanh Trường and the old xã Thanh Minh into phường Điện Biên Phủ, and merged xã Nà Nhạn, Pá Khoang, and Mường Phăng into xã Mường Phăng. The national tourism desk still prints the provincial capital as Thành phố Điện Biên Phủ. The museum and the relic board now print phường Điện Biên Phủ, tỉnh Điện Biên. Both the city wording and the 2025 ward wording stay.
dotReason: The 1954 basin is the reason to stop, on the far side of Pha Đin.
summary: A valley city in the far northwest, site of the famous 1954 battle, ringed by hills and rice fields. Climb Hill D1 to the victory monument, walk the battle hills and the Muong Thanh bridge, and try local dishes such as pa pinh top, folded grilled fish. One night suits history travellers.
timeNeeded: One night, or two if Mường Phăng is next
fee: Relic points are 20,000 VND. Museum pages print 100,000 VND and 5,000 VND.
getThere: Fly Hanoi–Điện Biên, 539 km or 453 km, or the road over Pha Đin. No station in the city.
bestMonths: March for ban flower; fog on Pha Đin in Dec–Feb
seoTitle: Dien Bien Phu guide — the 1954 basin after Pha Din
seoDescription: Stay for the 1954 monument in the Mường Thanh basin, not a Sơn La night and not Mộc Châu tea. Flights print 539 km and 453 km. Ban flower week moves.
intro: You are in the Mường Thanh basin, rice on the valley floor and a ring of hills around the town. The victory monument stands on Đồi D1. The 2021 handbook says it sits high enough to see the city, the yellow rice fields, and the ridges. Stay if that monument and this basin are the trip. Sleep in Sơn La if the night you wanted is the prison hill on the other side of Pha Đin. Sleep in Mộc Châu if you wanted the tea morning further east. This city is the basin after the pass. It is not the pass.

The bed is a small hotel or guesthouse in phường Điện Biên Phủ, near the monument and the Nậm Rốm. From 1 July 2025 that ward includes the old wards Him Lam, Tân Thanh, Mường Thanh, Thanh Bình, and Thanh Trường and the old xã Thanh Minh. The national tourism desk still says thành phố Điện Biên Phủ. No hotel brand is a pick. After dark the address with a 2026 page is Phố đi bộ Mường Thanh, beside the Nậm Rốm, in the block the city paper calls Khu đô thị mới – Chợ Du lịch Mường Thanh. The handbook also puts a cultural program on the monument yard on Saturday evenings and on holidays. Đồi A1 has a separate night opening on the relic board’s standing hours page. On 23 March 2026 the city paper said later evenings on the walking street were thin: a few drink stalls at the head of the street, most booths not yet trading. Do not expect a full night market every evening, and do not treat this street as the 2012 night market on Nguyễn Chí Thanh.

Give the morning to the monument, then A1, the De Castries bunker, and the Mường Thanh bridge, and leave the museum on its own ticket. The relic gates open at 7:00. They shut from 11:00 to 13:30, then open again until 18:00 in the spring-summer block or 17:30 in the autumn-winter block. Arriving at noon wastes the hills. Mường Phăng is the next morning, not a second city: 40 km by road from the center, about 10 km when the sentence is Highway 6, and 17 km only as a straight line. Do not add those into one drive. The mistake is booking Sơn La or Mộc Châu when the monument is the reason you stopped, or paying the relic’s 20,000 VND point ticket and assuming it covers the museum.
gettingAround: The nearest airport is Cảng hàng không Điện Biên, IATA DIN. Vietnam Airlines’ Hanoi-to-Điện Biên page calls it Cảng hàng không quốc tế Điện Biên, in phường Thanh Trường, thành phố Điện Biên Phủ, about 4 km from the center. The same airline’s return page calls it Cảng hàng không Điện Biên Phủ, at Tổ dân phố 10, phường Thanh Trường, also about 4 km. The national tourism desk still says sân bay Mường Thanh in thành phố Điện Biên Phủ, and the relic board’s pass article also says sân bay Mường Thanh. Thanh Trường is inside phường Điện Biên Phủ from 1 July 2025. Vietnam Airlines’ note of 4 March 2026 says that airline was flying Hanoi–Điện Biên twice a day and added flights for Ban flower week. No second airline is named on that note. There is no rail station in the city. The tourism desk’s transport lines, the relic board, and the airline pages do not name one.

By air from Hanoi (HAN) to DIN, the outbound airline page prints about 1 hour 15 minutes, 539 km, and 2 flights a day. The return page prints about 1 hour 5 minutes, 453 km, and about 1–2 flights a day. The national tourism desk prints about one hour. All three durations stay, and both distances stay. A single timetable for one day was not frozen. Fares move. Check on arrival. For Ban flower week 2026, Vietnam Airlines said it added return flights on 19, 21, 22, 24, and 26 March 2026, and extra flights on 6 and 8 March 2026, on top of 2 a day. That is a March 2026 notice, not the ordinary week.

From the airport to the monument, the return airline page prints 10–15 minutes for about 4 km. A second commercial page prints about 4.1 km and 8–10 minutes. Taxi on the return page is 70,000–80,000 VND, and a motorbike taxi on that page is 50,000 VND. The other page prints a taxi around 80,000 VND and a motorbike taxi at 40,000–60,000 VND. Those are airline and commercial pages, not a city tariff. A taxi fare inside the ward is check on arrival.

By road from Hanoi, the national tourism desk prints 478 km, National Highway 279 then National Highway 6, and does not print a duration. Commercial coach pages print about 400 km and about 10 hours, and 453 km and 15 hours. All three kilometer figures stay, and both hour figures stay. Bến xe Mỹ Đình lists Chi nhánh Hà Nội – Công ty TNHH HVĐB to Điện Biên Phủ at 19:30, 20:15, 20:45, and 21:15, with fares printed as 460,000–565,000–700,000 VND. Other commercial clocks and fares disagree with that row. The fare on the day is check on arrival.

Pha Đin is the pass on the Sơn La road. It is not this city. The relic board prints the pass as 32 km on National Highway 6, and a post-2005 alignment along the old road’s left slope as 26 km. Height is more than 1,000 m on the relic board and on the tourism desk. GoVietnam prints the summit at 1,648 m. From this city the relic board says nearly 100 km in the opening sentence and about 84 km to the end of the pass. GoVietnam says 80 km to the summit. From Sơn La town the relic board says the start is 66 km west. GoVietnam says 65 km from Sơn La. These pairs are not a door-to-door total. Do not add them. GoVietnam prints 2–2.5 hours from this city to the summit. Minutes on the relic board are check on arrival. One commercial coach page prints 160 km and 10 hours between this city and Sơn La. That 160 km is a separate commercial figure, not the pass pairs above. A road-authority minute count is check on arrival.

National Highway 279 inside the province runs from Tuần Giáo through the city to the Tây Trang border gate, 117 km on the tourism desk. That 117 km is not the drive from Sơn La and not the drive from Hanoi. National Highway 12 is 195 km from the city to the Ma Lu Thàng border gate, which the desk places in Lai Châu. That is the gate, not the kilometer to Lai Châu city. Mộc Châu sits on Highway 6 before Sơn La, on the way to Hanoi. A kilometer from this city is check on arrival. Hòa Bình is on that road before Mộc Châu. A kilometer from here is check on arrival. A time for a road or a flight that ends in Sa Pa was not printed. Check on arrival. Mường Lay is a town of the province on the tourism desk’s older list, and the 2026 flower plan names a white-Thái house day there. A time from this ward is check on arrival. Tuần Giáo is the district town on the pass road. Pha Đin’s Điện Biên side is in Tuần Giáo on the relic board. The 117 km figure includes the city and Tây Trang. It is not a Tuần Giáo-to-monument kilometer.

The monument, the museum, A1, the bunker, and the bridge sit in the basin ward. Him Lam is on đường Võ Nguyên Giáp, the old road 41, toward Tuần Giáo. A length for that renamed road is check on arrival. Mường Phăng is 40 km by road from the center, 17 km in a straight line, or about 10 km from Highway 6, depending on the sentence. The cannon-pull road at old xã Nà Nhạn is about 14 km from the city center on the handbook, beside Highway 279. That commune is inside xã Mường Phăng from 1 July 2025. A city bus map and a motorbike hire price are check on arrival. The airport transfer fares above are not a fare inside town.

On the pass, GoVietnam names thick fog in December–February and tells drivers to avoid June–August rain, and it prints 14–22°C at the summit. That temperature is one commercial page, not a city weather station. The relic board does not print a closure calendar. A pass-closure notice is check on arrival. Relic day hours change on 1 March and 1 October.

stayAreas.name: Basin ward
stayAreas.summary: Small hotels and guesthouses in phường Điện Biên Phủ, near the victory monument and the Nậm Rốm. From 1 July 2025 the ward includes the old wards Him Lam, Tân Thanh, Mường Thanh, Thanh Bình, and Thanh Trường and the old xã Thanh Minh. No hotel brand is a pick. A room rate is check on arrival.

eat: The culture desk’s nine are pa pỉnh tộp, cáy pỉnh, xôi nếp nương, steamed black chicken, ban flower, bitter bamboo, pork in leaves, bon soup, and hearth-dried meat. Bản Phiêng Lơi is the hamlet table at the city entrance. A price is Check on arrival.

Vietnam News adds kitchen-smoked buffalo, duck with banana flower, cabbage-wrapped oleaster, and chẩm chéo. Vietnamnet adds sâu chít, gạo tám, and bánh dày. Bamboo worms, Mông wine, mountain goat, and Đà River fish are named without a method. Market hours are Check on arrival.
interestsBody: The night is the basin under the monument. The hills of 1954, the Nậm Rốm, and the forest headquarters at Mường Phăng are the reasons the day splits the way it does. Sơn La is the valley on the other side of Pha Đin. Mộc Châu is the tea plateau further east.

The culture desk’s nine for this province are pa pỉnh tộp, cáy pỉnh, xôi nếp nương Điện Biên, gà đen hấp, nộm rau ban, măng đắng, nhứa phò, canh bon, and nhứa giảng. Bản Phiêng Lơi is the hamlet table at the city entrance. Pa pỉnh tộp is folded grilled fish: the culture desk says cooks use a fish of 1–1.5 kg, open it along the back, salt it, and stuff it with mắc khén, roasted fresh chili, spring onion, herbs, and coriander, then clamp it with bamboo. Vietnam News names chẩm chéo as a sauce beside the fish. The culture desk does not use those words in the recipe. Cáy pỉnh is chicken grilled after local herbs, wrapped in lemongrass leaves, skin crisp, the meat smelling of mắc khén, with a cup of rice wine the page calls “chén rượu” and does not name. Xôi nếp nương is upland sticky rice steamed twice, colored red, purple, yellow, and green by leaves, tubers, and fruit the page does not name. A ball of it leaves the hand clean. The packet is not cơm lam. Cơm lam is not in the nine. Gà đen hấp is steamed black chicken from Tủa Chùa, a Hmong bird on the culture page, not a basin-market breakfast. Nộm rau ban is young ban flower and leaves, in March when the culture desk says the flower is on the passes. Măng đắng is forest bamboo with a sweet-bitter taste. Nhứa phò is minced pork shoulder wrapped in leaves and grilled until the leaf is dry at the edge and the meat is the yellow the culture desk describes. Canh bon is a Thái soup of buffalo or beef skin, sweet dọc bon, wild eggplant, herbs, mắc khén, and lemongrass. Nhứa giảng is meat dried over a wood fire, usually buffalo, pork, and beef, still red and hot. Vietnam News also names kitchen-smoked buffalo. Whether that is the same cut is check on arrival. The same news page names bamboo worms, Mông wine, mountain goat, and Đà River fish. A method was not in that paragraph. Stall prices, market clocks, and a breakfast hour are check on arrival. No restaurant is a pick.

interestCards.summary: For the copper group on Đồi D1 and the rice in the basin under it.

interestCards.title: The hills of 1954
interestCards.summary: For A1, Him Lam, the bunker, and the museum, on the relic day hours.

interestCards.title: The river evening

interestGroups.title: The monument over the rice
interestGroups.summary: For the copper group on Đồi D1, and the rice and the Nậm Rốm under it.

cards.title: The Nam Rom
cards.summary: The river through the ward, and the rice the handbook sees from Đồi D1. Not a tea plateau.

body: The handbook treats Đồi D1 as the eastern outpost of the Dominique group and puts the copper monument there so the view takes in the city, the yellow rice, and the ridges. The group is three soldiers and one Thái child. The flag reads “Quyết chiến, quyết thắng.” The sculptor is Nguyễn Hải. The ceremony yard is about 3,000 m² on the handbook, used for cultural programs on Saturday evenings and on holidays. The 2022 route page says this is the copper monument in the 50th-anniversary works and that the group weighs 217 tons. The handbook does not print 217 tons. The weight stays on the route page. The yard size stays on the handbook. They are not one measurement. The same route page calls the hill a peace park with a view over the city. A visit length on the hill was not printed. Check on arrival. The relic board charges 20,000 VND a person a visit a point for visitors 18 and over. Ethnic residents of the province, older people, and people with severe disability pay half. Veterans, people with a revolutionary-service paper, organized students and soldiers with a plan, people under 18, and people with especially severe disability are free. A 2024 provincial television note says the electronic receipt runs at four points, and the monument is one of them. Whether the yard and the hill are one point or two is check on arrival. The national tourism desk calls Mường Thanh the largest basin in the Northwest.

The victory museum is a separate ticket. The museum’s own page, citing Nghị quyết 13/2024/NQ-HĐND of 4 November 2024 and Công văn 5076/UBND-KT of 11 November 2024, charges 100,000 VND a visit a person from age 18, Vietnamese or foreign. Half price for ethnic residents of the province, older people, people named in the cultural-access decision, and people with severe disability. Free under 18, veterans, organized students and soldiers with a plan, and people with especially severe disability. The ticket is that day only and is not refunded. The national tourism desk prints 5,000 VND a person for one of five sites at the museum. Both figures stay. The gate on the day is check on arrival. The museum footer prints Tổ dân phố Mường Thanh, phường Điện Biên Phủ. The ticket desk prints Tổ 1, phường Điện Biên Phủ. The national tourism desk still prints Phố 1, P. Mường Thanh, TP. Điện Biên Phủ. The tourism desk says the building opened in 1984 for the 30th anniversary, was reworked at the end of 2003, and then had five galleries, 274 objects, and 122 paintings. The museum’s 2026 hours notice does not repeat those counts. They are not a 2026 inventory. A panorama length was not printed.

The museum’s standing page says every day, summer 7:00–11:00 and 13:30–18:00, winter 7:00–11:00 and 13:30–17:30, and a separate Tết notice. From 13 July 2026 until a newer notice, the museum and the culture desk say 7:30–12:00 and 13:30–21:00. The national tourism desk prints 7:00–11:00 and 13:30–17:00. All three clocks stay. A visit length was not printed. Check on arrival. The relic’s 20,000 VND point ticket is not this museum’s ticket.

interestGroups.title: The hills of 1954
interestGroups.summary: For A1, Him Lam, the bunker, and the half day at Mường Phăng.

cards.title: Muong Thanh bridge
cards.summary: The Bailey span over the Nậm Rốm, 40 m by 5 m on the 2022 route page. The bridge is not in the four receipt points.

body: Đồi A1 watches the basin. The French name on the handbook is Eliane 2. The local names are Pú Lạng Chượng and Đồi Đồn Tây. The handbook says the fighting lasted 39 days and nights and more than 2,500 soldiers died. The 2022 route page repeats the 39 days and the 2,500, and adds a tank it calls 18 tons, the French bunker on the crest, the trench system, and a blast crater it calls 960 kg, restored in 2004 for the 50th anniversary. The handbook’s poem-page names the crater’s shape and does not print 960 kg or 18 tons. Both pages stay. Day hours, all week including holidays: from 1 March 2026 the relic board sets spring-summer, 1 March–30 September, at 7:00–11:00 and 13:30–18:00, and autumn-winter, 1 October–28 February, at 7:00–11:00 and 13:30–17:30. The standing hours page matches those day blocks, dates the winter pattern from 5 October 2022, and adds A1 at night, 19:30–21:30 on Friday, Saturday, and official holidays. The March 2026 notice does not mention the night. The night window stays. This page does not decide that the notice cancelled it. Báo Quảng Ninh says the lighting was finished in December 2024, the night opening started 1 January 2025, the project cost more than 13 billion VND, and the adult night ticket was 20,000 VND, matching the relic point fee. The two 20,000 VND lines do not say whether a day ticket covers the night. A walk length is check on arrival. Noon is closed on both the 2026 notice and the standing page.

The De Castries bunker is the heart of the French command on the handbook, which prints the flag on the roof at 17:30 on 7 May 1954. The 2022 route page uses the same “heart” line and does not repeat 17:30. The Mường Phăng page’s 15:00 order on 7 May is the assault order at the forest headquarters, not this flag minute. Both moments stay. From this stop the handbook says visitors can also see the Mường Thanh bridge, burned-out tanks left in place, and French 105 mm and 155 mm gun positions. Those guns are not separate stops. The bunker is 20,000 VND a person a visit a point if it is charged as its own point. The 2024 television note names Hầm Đờ Cát as one of the four electronic-receipt points. The March 2026 notice does not add a night opening here. The bridge the 2022 route page says the French called Bailey crosses the Nậm Rốm. That page prints the length as 40 m and the width as 5 m, and says the soldiers crossed it on the afternoon of 7 May 1954. The handbook names the bridge beside the bunker and does not print 40 m or 5 m. The four named receipt points do not include the bridge. A bridge ticket is check on arrival. Do not assume the 20,000 VND point fee applies.

Him Lam, Béatrice on the handbook, is the outer strongpoint on the old road 41, now đường Võ Nguyên Giáp, the northeast gate toward Tuần Giáo. The assault started at 17:00 on 13 March 1954 and the position fell at 23:30 the same day. The handbook names Phan Đình Giót. The culture desk’s 2026 flower note adds the inauguration of the phase-two conservation project on 9 March 2026. The 13 March date is the 1954 battle, not a festival calendar. A trench length is check on arrival. The 20,000 VND point line applies if the gate charges Him Lam as its own point. Him Lam is not in the four-point television list. Whether this gate sells that ticket is check on arrival. A kilometer from the monument is check on arrival.

Hill E is the veterans’ center on the eastern Dominique hills. The handbook says it was built for the 50th anniversary in 2004 as a Thái stilt-house gallery with 106 gifts. The 2022 route page says people come to offer incense for Hồ Chí Minh and the dead. Hill F, Mont Fictif on the handbook, is immediately east of A1. The handbook says the memorial was started on 13 March 2021 on 4.95 ha, with a wooden temple, a still court, and a pool, then expected to open in 2022. The route page expected the inauguration on 7 May 2022. On 4 May 2026 the relic board lists Đồi F and the memorial among the points that were receiving visitors. That May note is a holiday staffing plan, not a new clock. Fees for E and F are check on arrival. They are not in the four-point list. The special national relic has 45 component points. Độc Lập is in that catalog at xã Thanh Nưa, huyện Điện Biên, with no kilometer and no separate visitor note. It is not a stop on this page.

Mường Phăng is the forest command used from 31 January 1954 to 15 May 1954. The handbook says more than 20 huts and shelters have been rebuilt, including Võ Nguyên Giáp’s hut and the tunnel through the hill. The 2020 article prints that tunnel as 69 m and the forest area as about 90 km². The handbook does not print 69 m or 90 km². The general attack order went out at 15:00 on 7 May 1954. The parade ground at Phiêng Tá Lét, on 13 May 1954, has a later monument of 25 figures and six flags. Use 40 km by road when the sentence is the city center, about 10 km when the sentence is Highway 6, and 17 km only as the straight line. From 1 July 2025, xã Mường Phăng is the merged commune of Nà Nhạn, Pá Khoang, and Mường Phăng, not a ward of the basin. The lookout on Pú Tó Cọ is 1,700 m on the handbook, and the visit there is a footpath of more than 4 km from bản Khá, not a drive to the hut. A path length inside the forest, beyond those two figures, is check on arrival. The headquarters is one of the four receipt points, at the relic’s 20,000 VND point rate. Hồ Pá Khoang is the lake near Mường Phăng, with cherry blossom in spring and Thái houses beside the relic. The handbook does not print a kilometer from the basin. A boat, a beach, or a resort name was not printed. The cannon-pull road at Nà Nhạn is the short stop about 14 km toward Mường Phăng. The handbook names Tô Vĩnh Diện. Do not confuse that 14 km stop with Pha Đin. A 2018 holiday-waiver list named this road among seven sites, for ethnic residents of the province, and said the waiver lasted until the council amended an older fee resolution. The current relic fee page does not repeat that waiver. This page does not publish 7 May as free.

The evening, when it is on, is Phố đi bộ Mường Thanh beside the Nậm Rốm. The street opened on the evening of 7 March 2026 during Ban flower week. The city paper does not print an opening or a closing hour. One trader said weekday trade was afternoon and evening, and the weekend ran through the day. That is one trader’s clock, not a bylaw. The 2012 tourism-desk note describes a different night market on Nguyễn Chí Thanh, from the Trần Đăng Ninh junction to the provincial youth-house crossing, 580 m, about 4,500 m², nearly 90 temporary stalls and more than 160 households, open daily 20:00–23:30. Whether that 2012 market still opens is check on arrival. The Saturday yard under the monument is about 3,000 m². The handbook says it holds cultural programs on Saturday evenings and on holidays. A start and an end were not printed. A ranked bar street was not named. The hour the ward goes quiet was not printed.

Shopping, as far as the pages go, is the walking street’s plan for local goods, OCOP, and highland cloth, and Trung tâm thương mại Him Lam Plaza. The 2018 television survey names that plaza in the old phường Tân Thanh as one of two rank-III trade centers in the province. Most booths on the walking street were not yet trading on 23 March 2026. Chợ Trung tâm I is the city’s wholesale market on that 2018 survey, in the old phường Tân Thanh, now inside phường Điện Biên Phủ. A later city-paper piece says the market opened in 1992 with 150 kiosks. Neither page prints an opening hour. What is on the breakfast table is check on arrival. No shop is a pick. A resort property is not named as a reason to sleep here.

faqs.q: How do I get from Hanoi to Dien Bien Phu?
faqs.a: By air, the outbound Vietnam Airlines page prints about 1 hour 15 minutes and 539 km, with 2 flights a day. The return page prints about 1 hour 5 minutes and 453 km, with about 1–2 flights a day. The national tourism desk prints about one hour. By road, that desk prints 478 km via Highway 279 then Highway 6. Commercial coach pages print about 400 km and about 10 hours, and 453 km and 15 hours. Fares move. Check on arrival. There is no rail station in the city.

faqs.q: How far is Pha Din from Dien Bien Phu and from Son La?
faqs.a: The relic board prints the pass as 32 km, and a post-2005 alignment as 26 km, at more than 1,000 m. GoVietnam prints the summit at 1,648 m. From this city the relic board says nearly 100 km and about 84 km to the end of the pass. GoVietnam says 80 km to the summit, and 2–2.5 hours. From Sơn La the relic board says 66 km to the start. GoVietnam says 65 km. These pairs are not one total. A separate commercial page prints 160 km and 10 hours between the two cities. A road-authority minute count is check on arrival.

faqs.q: What does the victory museum cost, and when is it open?
faqs.a: The museum’s own page charges 100,000 VND a visit from age 18. The national tourism desk prints 5,000 VND a person for one of five sites at the museum. Both stay. The standing page says summer 7:00–11:00 and 13:30–18:00, and winter 7:00–11:00 and 13:30–17:30. From 13 July 2026 the museum and the culture desk say 7:30–12:00 and 13:30–21:00. The tourism desk prints 7:00–11:00 and 13:30–17:00. The gate on the day is check on arrival. The relic’s 20,000 VND point ticket does not cover this museum.

faqs.q: Is 7 May still free for ethnic residents of the province?
faqs.a: A 2018 culture-desk note waived fees for ethnic residents of the province on Tết (3 days), 2 September, 30 April, 1 May, and 7 May, at seven named sites, until the council amended an older resolution. The current relic fee page does not repeat that waiver. Whether 7 May is still free for those residents is check on arrival. The 17:30 flag on the De Castries bunker and the 15:00 order at Mường Phăng are two moments on 7 May 1954, not two festival clocks.

season.label: Ban flower in March
season.note: Ban flower week is yearly, in the middle of March, tied to the opening of the attack on 13 March 1954. In 2026 the province first planned 20–26 March, then moved the week to 6–12 March when the blossom moved, with the opening at 20:10 on Sunday 8 March 2026 at the provincial stadium in phường Điện Biên Phủ. The press note of 26 February 2026 says the main events sit in that ward. The civil dates for 2027 are check on arrival. On the road, GoVietnam’s pass page names thick fog in December–February and tells drivers to avoid June–August rain, and it prints 14–22°C at the summit. That temperature is one commercial page, not a city weather station. A pass-closure notice is check on arrival. Relic day hours change on 1 March and 1 October: spring-summer runs to 18:00, autumn-winter to 17:30, and the gates shut from 11:00 to 13:30.
